# Platform support: toolchain pages

<!-- Generated by tools/collect_results.py; don't edit by hand (see CLAUDE.md). -->

> One page per platform × compiler × architecture, each listing every documented feature and example with ✅ passed, ❌ failed, ⏭ skipped (with the reason) or — not run. The summary, the feature support matrix and the compiler and platform bugs found are on the entry page, [`../platform-support.md`](../platform-support.md).

The goal is every documented feature and every example on every supported platform, architecture and compiler, so the results show how far each toolchain supports modern C++. GitHub Actions runs are manual, each with the owner's consent; the local runs are the owner's machine and the `gcc:16` Docker image.

## What's in this folder

| Path | What | Edited by |
|---|---|---|
| `<platform>-<arch>-<compiler>.md` | One toolchain's results (names stay the same across runs) | generated |
| `local-<platform>-<arch>-<compiler>.md` | The same for a local run | generated |
| [`runs/<run-id>/`](runs/) | Each consented run's `results-*.json` and `run.json` (date, commit, inputs, jobs); never logs. The report is rebuilt from here after GitHub's retention runs out (runs: 41380889279, 41393465801) | the collector |
| [`local/`](local/) | The local results used, with `local.json` (date, commit) | you, then the collector |
| [`known-bugs.json`](known-bugs.json) | Compiler and platform bugs: upstream link, repo issue, affected toolchains | by hand, validated |
| `README.md` | This index | generated |

## Regenerating

After a consented run, follow the [`platform-support`](../../.claude/skills/platform-support/SKILL.md) skill: process every log, capture the findings in the tests, then

```bash
tools/collect_results.py <run-id>…          # the latest run of every platform workflow
tools/collect_results.py <run-id>… --check  # nothing stale
```

It rewrites this folder, the entry page and the README's "Tested platforms" table. Details: [`docs/testing.md`](../testing.md).
